aggregation: 4 distinct recordings/dataset, clean/noisy; equal recording means and equal dataset macro. Dev/confirmation disjoint VAL recordings, 2/dataset. Not full VAL or TEST.

conclusion.near_only: No consistent practical gain: macro World clean +0.0050mm/noisy -0.0225mm, RICH +0.0019/+0.0008mm; PA and foot differences tiny/mixed. The broad-only feedback-permission hypothesis is not supported as a dominant error source in this frozen head-only cohort.
conclusion.feedback_off: Small and inconsistent benefit: macro World clean -0.9825mm/noisy -0.0462mm; RICH World -0.3275/-0.5831mm and PA -0.4719/-0.2755mm, but RICH foot-height absolute error worsens +1.9552/+2.8745mm. Not a reliable solution to floating or foot sliding.
conclusion.scene_gain_location: Most of the baseline scene benefit survives learned-feedback removal, supporting scene conditioning in the generator as a major contributor in this cohort. This experiment does not separate global/local/relation conditioning and does not prove feedback can be removed during retraining without consequence.
conclusion.near_only_semantics: Original 67-anchor query valid across 0.08/0.25/0.60m scales is aggregated to region_valid for feedback only. Query centers can blend reliable tracks; relation_only does not mean every scene point is physically farther than 0.6m from the predicted body. Scene context, BPS and query validity are retained.
conclusion.limits: No training or inference-weight changes; fixed12-window VAL panel only. Small changes do not establish statistical significance or justify automatic architecture promotion. Foot height is GT joint-height error, not scene penetration measurement.
